chunks: As for your women who have lost hope of menstruation, and in case you have a doubt, the prescribed period (of waiting) for them is three months, as also for those who have not menstruated yet. As for those who are pregnant, their prescribed period is until the delivery of the child. God will make things easy for him who is mindful of God.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a woman who has reached menopause or is pregnant according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This verse (Ayat al-Iddah) establishes the legal framework for the waiting period (iddah) in divorce, specifically addressing the ambiguity surrounding women who have reached menopause or are prepubescent by assigning them a fixed three-month period. It further clarifies that for pregnant women, the iddah extends until childbirth, linking the end of the waiting period to the physical reality of delivery. The verse concludes with a spiritual promise that God-consciousness (taqwa) brings ease, a theme often cited in Shia jurisprudence to connect legal rulings with spiritual devotion.
